overview: Brazil is the largest country in South America and the fifth-largest in the world. Its capital is Brasília, a planned city built in the late 1950s, while São Paulo is its largest city. Brazil was a Portuguese colony until it became independent in 1822, and it is now the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world. Its men's team has won the football World Cup five times, more than any other country.

geography.text: Most of the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth, lies in Brazil, crossed by the Amazon river and its many tributaries. South of the Amazon are the high plains of central Brazil, covered in a tropical savanna called the cerrado. Brazil has a very long Atlantic coastline, and in the south-west the Pantanal is one of the largest tropical wetlands in the world.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mostly tropical, with the hot, wet Amazon in the north and cooler winters in the south.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Amazon and the Pantanal wetlands hold jaguars, capybaras, macaws and pink river dolphins.

history.text: Indigenous peoples lived in Brazil for thousands of years before Portugal claimed it in 1500 and brought millions of enslaved Africans to work its plantations and mines. Brazil became independent in 1822 as an empire, abolished slavery in 1888, the last country in the Americas to do so, and became a republic in 1889. After military rule from 1964 to 1985, it returned to democracy.

events.title: Portuguese arrival
events.text: Pedro Álvares Cabral claims Brazil for Portugal.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Brazil declares independence as an empire.

events.title: Slavery abolished
events.text: Brazil becomes the last country in the Americas to end slavery.

events.title: Republic
events.text: The emperor is overthrown and Brazil becomes a republic.

events.title: Brasília
events.text: A new capital is opened in the interior.

government.text: Brazil is a federal presidential republic of 26 states and a federal district, where the capital, Brasília, stands. The President is elected every four years and is head of state and government. Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate. Voting is compulsory for adults aged 18 to 70.

economy.text: Brazil has the largest economy in Latin America. It is the world's top exporter of soybeans, coffee, sugar, orange juice and beef, and a major producer of iron ore and oil. It also builds aircraft through Embraer. Most of its electricity comes from hydropower.

culture.text: Brazil is the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world. Its culture blends Indigenous, African and European roots. Rio de Janeiro's Carnival is one of the biggest parties on Earth, and Brazil gave the world samba and bossa nova music. The Amazon rainforest covers about 60% of the country.

items.title: Carnival
items.text: Samba schools parade through Rio's Sambadrome every year.

items.title: Christ the Redeemer
items.text: The 30-metre statue above Rio, finished in 1931.

items.title: Capoeira
items.text: A martial art mixed with dance and music, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Feijoada, a black bean stew with pork, is the national dish; pão de queijo cheese bread is a favourite snack.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Samba, bossa nova and funk music, and a huge TV soap opera industry.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Carnival, before Lent, is celebrated with parades, music and dancing across the country.

sport.text: Football is a national obsession. Brazil has won the men's World Cup five times, more than any other country, and has produced legends such as Pelé, Ronaldo and Marta. Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics, the first in South America.

items.text: A record five men's World Cups.

items.title: Pelé
items.text: The only player to win three World Cups.
Rio hosted the first Olympics in South America.

didYouKnow: Brazil is named after brazilwood, a tree once used to make red dye.
Brazil shares a border with every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

keyPeople.name: Pelé
keyPeople.text: The only player to win three World Cups.

keyPeople.name: Marta
keyPeople.text: Has scored more World Cup goals than any other player, man or woman.
